title: My Elephant
paragraphs: I slip into the room silently and reveal myself.
“I’m home!”
“Welcome home!”
“Welcome home, Kitamura!”
Yuki-chan and Kou greeted me cheerfully. To see the joyful faces of Filolial-sama and the others when I return after finishing a job… it truly is the greatest reward for The Love Hunter.
“It seems Father and the others haven’t come home yet.”
“That’s right. It’s been quite a while, hasn’t it?”

Yuki-chan checks outside through the window. That flashy mammoth is probably giving Father and the others a lengthy tour of the mansion. I can easily imagine that. Frankly, it’s a huge mistake to take up Father’s time—who’s already so busy—just for your sake, but since security has been thinned out because of it, I’ll make an exception. Now then…
“Kou.”
I turn to Kou and ask.
“What?”
“Do you like elephants, Kou?”
“Yeah.”
“How much do you like them?”
“Hmm?”
Kou tilts her head slightly and stares at me. I look back at her earnestly.
“What do you mean?”
“I’m asking if you like Zou enough to marry her someday.”
“Hmm…?”
“I’m asking if you’d be okay with Zou belonging to Father.”
“Hmm? Elmero is under Iwatani’s command, right?”
Judging by this reaction, it seems Kou’s feelings for Zou are similar to those of Big Sister and her friends. I was a little worried, but it turned out to be a needless concern.
“I see. No problem then.”
“I don’t get it at all!”
Countless question marks are floating above Kou’s head.
“Kou is still just a kid, isn’t he?”
“Boo! I’m not a kid!”
Kou is getting all worked up over Yuki-chan’s words. It’s a heartwarming sight.
“The time will come when Kou understands, too. That time you tried to pick someone up was just practice, after all.”
“Is that so? Kou, trying to pick up Elmero? Hmm?”

It seems Kou still doesn’t quite get it. Well, I suppose Kou’s love life is still a long way off. After all, the type of person Kou falls for is a bit off the mark by standard worldly standards. I can’t even begin to imagine what kind of person he’ll fall in love with next. Well then, let’s go explain this to Father.
So, with that in mind, I started practicing Idol choreography with Yuki-chan and the others until Father and the others returned. As I thought about that, I struck the Filolial Mask victory pose.
“I see. So that’s how it was… I had a vague idea, but…”

After a while, Father and the others returned after finishing their tour with Kebamammoth. Apparently, Kebamammoth had originally intended to tag along and ask all sorts of probing questions right up until dinner, but it seemed like Panda and Éclair stepped in at just the right moment to bring them back. Then, to make sure no one eavesdropped, Yuki-chan and the others worked together to keep watch and use Magic to keep the conversation private. The topic, of course, was an explanation of the situation regarding the elephant.
“It’s a bit awkward for me to say this, since I’m the one who let him in, but the Elmero family is complicated, isn’t it?”
“How should I put it… it’s the opposite pattern of Lars-chan’s, isn’t it?”
“……That’s true.”
Panda furrows his brow slightly, but doesn’t seem to disagree.

“Family background and bloodlines can be a troublesome thing at times… Even among the nobles of Melromarc, there are rare cases where Demi-Humans are born, and I’ve heard that those who are born that way end up in quite a miserable situation.”
So there are similar stories floating around in Melromarc as well. With so many twisted nobles in that country, I suppose it can’t be helped.
“In Melromarc’s case… perhaps it’s the result of a noblewoman’s reckless dalliance—a dangerous romance with a slave or the like?”

“If it were a problem caused by the person themselves, that would still be better. But if, by some stroke of luck, a child resembling the mother were born from such a dalliance, and then several generations later…”

It’s easy to imagine a future where she’s cast out of her family for infidelity she never committed. Or perhaps they’ll just pin the blame on a slave or something and have them executed. Since Melromarc is a country where pigs hold the upper hand, it seems the pigs are often let off the hook for their misdeeds. It makes me want to vomit.

By the way, according to Father from the first world, the reason Melromarc favors pigs is that it was founded by a pig who posed as the wife of a past Hero—or something like that. Apparently, the Crimson Swine itself interferes quite a bit, too.
“Ah… so that’s a possibility, huh. I’d assumed the child would be something like half-and-half.”

“There are all sorts of mysteries around here. By the way, according to Siltvelt lore, when the Shield Hero has a child with a Demi-Human, Beastman, the Demi-Human, Beastman blood is said to be strong and not diluted.”
“No, I didn’t want to know that.”

Father is furrowing his brow deeply and looking troubled. Hmm… Is that Father’s child? I can only remember it very vaguely. I do remember, though, that the child of Itsuki and the Stalker Pig was hyperactive despite having a negative personality.
“I see… So Elmero had foster parents who cherished him, huh?”
“I can understand the feeling of cherishing one’s foster parents.”
After all, Panda’s stepfather is a peacock Beastman. He probably understands that blood isn’t everything.
“From this family’s perspective, Elmero—who’s achieved unexpected success and risen to the rank of my close aide—is… a thorn in their side, I suppose?”

“That’s probably the case. They’ve already failed in their attempts to win over Lord Iwatani and been sidelined, and now someone they’d rather not even count as family has risen through the ranks. It’s hard to cut ties, but they can’t just let things stay this way.”
“So I guess they’re trying to find a way to replace him as a close aide… How short-sighted. Elmero should just tell him off.”
That’s how Panda wrapped it up.
All right, now’s the time!
Let’s give Zou a big push with Father. Now I can see a bright future ahead.

“So, Father! Let me speak from my own experience as a pig: if you tell Zou, ‘Do your best!’ or ‘I like you!’ or ‘You’re my Zou!’ then Zou will rebel against the family, and everything will work out smoothly!”
“Coming from Motoyasu-kun’s track record… I mean, if it works out, great… but… hmm.”
Father is crossing his arms and grumbling with a slightly skeptical look on his face. Is something off here? When it was my turn, things usually worked out just like this, didn’t they?
“Well, pigs and elephants are genetically different, after all.”
“No, that’s not what I meant…”
“Anyway, it’s all about momentum. Your passion can turn everything upside down.”
“Hmm… Well, I mean, I can sort of understand the sentiment? I’ll take your advice into consideration, though.”
“To begin with, I find it hard to agree with the way Lord Kitamura phrased that… I mean, what does he think women are…?”
Éclair seems to have some doubts as well. This isn’t going over well at all. What exactly is so wrong with elephants?
“Well, since it’s just a tactic that worked on pigs, I can understand why it’s difficult.”
“In that sense… no, never mind.”
“As always, things get complicated when the Spear Hero gets involved, don’t they?”
“If Lord Motoyasu said something like that to me, Yuki would give it her all to break through no matter what!”

Yuki-chan actually backed my idea here! I mean, she does have a certain air about her—like she’s part of the nobility or comes from a wealthy family. And with that air of refinement, there’s no doubt she’s nobility!
“I get that you’re all fired up… but hey, just give me a sec. I’ve got a few tricks up my sleeve, too. Or rather… it looks like the other guy might just shoot himself in the foot.”

It seems Father has a plan of his own. Apparently, despite being a brainless musclehead by family lineage, he’s trying to use his head—but there are plenty of holes in his reasoning. So, we kept chatting until dinner was served.

And so, it was time for dinner. We were led to a room inside the mansion with a large dining table. The table, which was quite high, was piled high with food. It gave the impression of being mostly vegetables. I wonder who prepared this… probably the rat-beastmen and the slaves, right?
Anyway, the entire Mammoth family was seated together. Zou… was made to sit in the most inconspicuous seat, farthest away from Father. He looked a bit downcast.
“Elmero, Kou, I’d like to sit next to you.”
Seeing how anxious the Elephant looked, Kou volunteered to sit next to him. Aww, you’ve really grown up, Kou. It’s a world of difference from when you were making a fuss about wanting to eat moles.
“…Well then, I’ll make room. In exchange, I’ll take your seat.”

And just as if she’d been waiting for this moment, the Flashy Mammoth has Kou make room for the seat he was supposed to occupy, moving closer to Father. She must have judged that moving slightly closer to Father would give her an advantage. Without saying a word, the Mammoth family coordinated with just a glance and naturally switched seats. They’re maintaining a stance of aggressively courting Father. By the way, I was annoyed that the Flashy Mammoth took Kou’s seat.
“Well then…”

With that, they began the traditional Siltvelt meal prayer. I suppose he’s a devout believer, at least on the surface. Even if he’s got something up his sleeve. Father also seemed accustomed to the routine and joined in the prayer. And so, a meal began that appeared harmonious yet was tinged with a subtle sense of tension.
“Is this the Elmero family’s home-cooked flavor?”
Kou asked Zou as he ate the dish that had been served.
“Yes, it seems so.”
His reply was a bit odd. Well, maybe he just said it without thinking. Or perhaps mammoths rarely cook.
“Hmm… there’s a lot here. Can I have some more?”
“Yes, please.”

Zou transfers food from a large plate to a small one… and then to an even larger one, placing it in front of Kou so he can eat. Kou opens his mouth in sync with the spoon Zou holds, loaded with food, and eats. It’s quite heartwarming. For some reason, this scene makes me think Father from the first world would say it looks like a parent feeding its chick.

By the way, just as Kou’s reaction suggests, the taste is ordinary. From Kou’s perspective—having grown accustomed to Father’s cooking—it’s probably a bit underwhelming. Yet he seems to have acquired the restraint not to voice that. Kou’s growth knows no bounds. I’m starting to feel quite proud, too.
“Hehe… I wonder if Elmero is smitten with a child like that? You really ought to take good care of the Shield Hero.”
Kebamammoth seized the moment to put Kou in a favorable light by downplaying Zou. That’s annoying. Know your place.
Zou is silently feeding Kou while gazing at him gently.
“Hmm… Didn’t he like it?”
“No. Look, he’s spilling food.”
Zou takes out a handkerchief and holds it out in front of Kou. Kou takes it and wipes his mouth.
“So, Shield Hero, I hear you inspected the gardens on our estate today. How do you like the dishes made with produce harvested from those gardens?”
The elderly mammoth asks Father.
“I think it’s wonderful. The flavors of the ingredients really come through.”

Father replies without a hitch. Well… the flavors of the ingredients do come through clearly. That’s a standard phrase he uses when responding smoothly. In the first world, whenever Father ate truly delicious food, he’d just say, “Hmm…” and eat in silence. Or rather, as far as I know, he’s never offered a critique of a meal unless specifically asked to.
“Well, I’m truly delighted by this warm welcome.”

Father’s smile looks a bit forced. Is he up to something? Just thinking that I’ll get to see that scary Father again for the first time in a while gives me chills. Should I just go along with it and say, “Yes”? Yes.
“We, too, greatly appreciate that welcome.”
“What a blessing.”
The elderly Mammoth—presumably the representative of the Mammoth family—replies.
“So, we’d feel bad if we just accepted the welcome. That’s why… we’d like to show our appreciation as well… Elmero-san.”
“Y-yes. What is it?”
Zou responds to Father’s question.
“I believe you’re teaching Kou and Filolial and the others how to sing, right?”
“Y-yes.”

“Would it be okay if you performed one for us here? It’d be better than just eating, right? Having you play music or sing. Since you’re my Guardian Knight, Elmero, could I ask you to do this on your own, separate from your family duties?”

I get the feeling Father was trying to emphasize my role as his Guardian Knight. The Mammoth family also seems to have raised their eyebrows slightly at Father’s words. Father… isn’t this having the opposite effect? Zou is at a loss for words under the pressure from those around him.
“Elmero.”
At that moment, Kou takes Zou’s hand, as if to back him up. I heard later that Father had asked him beforehand to sing with Zou.
“Since it’s a request from Iwatani, let’s sing!”
“Kou…”
Zou looked at Kou, took a quiet, deep breath, and then nodded.
“All right. Then let’s sing.”
Zou, still holding hands with Kou, stood in front of the large, open fireplace at the back of the dining hall.
“Well then…”

He took a deep breath, waved his hand lightly—just as he had done while practicing the chorus with Filolial-sama and the others—and began to sing. Of course, Kou sang along too. His voice… was different from Filolial-sama’s—that crystal-clear, beautiful voice like a bird’s chirp—instead, it was a powerful, heart-stirring voice that resonated deeply, truly characteristic of Zou.

I see… It certainly seems that elephants do have a talent for music. I can see why the old mouse said so. That wonderful voice, the kind that would captivate anyone, continued for a while. Kou is singing along to support the elephant’s voice.
“This is… so elegant. I think Yuki should take a cue from this.”
Yuki-chan’s understanding of Idol shows has deepened recently. It looks like she’s about to take another step forward.
Zou is completely focused on singing. It seems his voice could carry on forever. I can tell he’s the type who gets completely absorbed in things once he’s engrossed.

Kou sang along, and soon they began dancing together… no, actually, Zou began performing a magnificent dance while Kou rode on his back. Zou naturally joined in, raising his hands and moving his trunk up and down… it was just like a scene from a musical. Even though it was just their singing, it almost sounded as if instruments were playing along.
That magical moment eventually came to an end. Zou quietly finished his song.
